small_guidance:
- The LN+GELU+scale kernel is fine but trivial — fast_p=0.22 means the ConvTranspose3d dominates. Tuning BLOCK_C/num_warps on the tail kernel cannot move the needle; at most try num_warps=2 since C=64 is tiny.
- If staying small, fuse the conv bias add into the LN kernel epilogue input (skip the separate bias add in cuDNN) by setting bias=False on the conv and adding bias inside ln_gelu_scale — minor win only.
large_guidance:
- Replace the ConvTranspose3d with a custom Triton scatter-add kernel: one program per (N, IC-tile, D_in-tile, H_in-tile, W_in-tile), compute the outer product input[n,ic,d,h,w] * weight[ic,oc,kd,kh,kw] and atomic-add into the output grid at (n, oc, d*stride+kd-pad, h*stride+kh-pad, w*stride+kw-pad). Handle stride=2, padding=1, kernel=4 explicitly in the index math.
- Alternatively, formulate as gather-GEMM: one program per (N, OC-tile, output-spatial-tile); loop over (ic, kd, kh, kw), gather the contributing input voxel (only when (out+pad-k) is divisible by stride and in-range), accumulate into a [BLOCK_OC, BLOCK_SP] tile. This avoids atomics. Output is channels-last so LN over OC=64 stays a contiguous reduction in the same kernel — fuse bias + LN + GELU + scale into the epilogue, eliminating two full tensor read/writes.
- Use channels_last memory layout end-to-end (permute weight to [OC, KD, KH, KW, IC] once at init); start autotune at BLOCK_OC=64 (full channel), BLOCK_SP=32 or 64, num_warps=4, num_stages=2, fp32. SMEM stays well under 132KB.
